verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              स प्रविश्य महाबाहुः पाण्डवानां निवेशनम्। पितामहीमभ्यवन्दत्साम्ना परमवल्गुना॥१॥
verses.english: Entering the palace of the Pandavas the mighty-armed prince saluted his grandmother in soothing and sweet words.

verses.sanskrit: ततश्चित्राङ्गदा देवी कौरव्यस्यात्मजापि च। पृथां कृष्णां च सहिते विनयेनोपजग्मतु॥२॥
verses.english: Then queen Chitrangada, and (Ulupi) the daughter of (the snake) Kauravya, together humbly approached Pritha and Krishna. They then met Subhadra and the other ladies of the Kuru race with due formalities.

verses.sanskrit: सुभद्रां च यथान्यायं याश्चान्याः कुरुयोषितः। ददौ कुन्ती ततस्ताभ्यां रत्नानि विविधानि च॥३॥
द्रौपदी च सुभद्रा च याश्चाप्यन्याऽददुः स्त्रियः। ऊषतुस्तत्र ते देव्यौ महार्हशयनासने॥४॥
verses.english: Kunti gave them many gems and costly things. Draupadi and Subha 'ra and the other ladies of Kuru's race all made presents to them.

verses.sanskrit: सु पूजिते स्वयं कुन्त्या पार्थस्य हितकाम्यया। स च राजा महातेजाः पूजितो बभ्रुवाहनः॥५॥
verses.english: The two ladies took up their residence there, using costly beds and seats, treated with affection and honor by Kunti herself from desire of doing what was agreeable to Partha.

verses.sanskrit: धृतराष्ट्रं महीपालमुपतस्थे यथाविधि। युधिष्ठिरं च राजानं भीमादींश्चापि पाण्डवान्॥६॥
verses.english: King Babhruvahana of great energy, duly honored (by Kunti), then inet Dhritarashtra according to due rites.

verses.sanskrit: उपगम्य महातेजा विनयेनाभ्यवादयत्। स तैः प्रेम्या परिष्वक्तः पूजितश्च यथाविधि॥७॥
verses.english: Going then to king Yudhishthira and Bhima and the other Pandavas the mighty prince of Munipura saluted them all with humility.

verses.sanskrit: धनं चास्मै ददुर्भूरि प्रीयमाणा महारथाः। तथैव च महीपाल: कृष्णं चक्रगदाधरम्॥८॥
verses.english: They all embraced him with great love and honored him duly. And those powerful carwarrior highly pleased with him, made large gifted of wealth to him.

verses.sanskrit: प्रद्युम्न इव गोविन्दं विनयेनोपतस्थिवान्। तस्मै कृष्णो ददौ राज्ञे महार्हमतिपूजितम्॥९॥
verses.english: The king of Manipura then humbly approached Krishna, that hero armed with the discus and the mace, like a second Pradyumna approaching his father. Krishna gave to the king a very costly and excellent car adorned with gold and to which were yoked excellent horses.

verses.sanskrit: रथं हेमपरिष्कारं दिव्याश्वयुजमुत्तमम्। धर्मराजश्च भीमश्च फाल्गुनश्च यमौ तथा॥१०॥
verses.english: Then king Yudhishthira the just, and Bhima, and Phalguna, and the twins, each separately honored him and made costly presents to him.

verses.sanskrit: पृथक् पृथक् च ते चैनं मानार्थाभ्यामयोजयन्। ततस्तृतीये दिवसे सत्यवत्यात्मजो मुनिः॥११॥
verses.english: On the third day, the sage Vyasa the son of Satyavati, that foremost of eloquent men, approaching Yudhishthira, said, From this day, O son of Kunti, do you begin your sacrifice. The time for it has come! The moment for undertaking the rite is at hand. The priests are urging you.

verses.sanskrit: युधिष्ठिरं समभ्येत्य वाग्मी वचनमब्रवीत्। अद्यप्रभृति कौन्तेय यजस्व समयो हि ते। मुहूर्तो यज्ञियः प्राप्तश्चोदयन्तीह याजकाः॥१२॥
अहीनो नाम राजेन्द्र क्रतुस्तेऽयं च कल्पताम्। बहुत्वात्काञ्चनाख्यस्य ख्यातो बहुसुवर्णकः॥१३॥
verses.english: Let the sacrifice be performed in such a way that no limb may become defective. On account of the very large quantity of gold that is required for this sacrifice, it has come to be called the sacrifice of profuse gold.

verses.sanskrit: एवमत्र महाराज दक्षिणां त्रिगुणां कुरु। त्रित्वं व्रजतु ते राजन्ब्राह्मणा ह्यत्र कारणम्॥१४॥
verses.english: Do you also, O great king, make the Dakshina of this sacrifice three times of what is enjoined. Let the merit of your sacrifice increase threefold. The Brahimanas competent for the purpose.
verses.bhavadeepa: अहीनः अह्नां सोमयागानां बहूनां समूहोऽहीनः न हीनः द्रव्यादिना इति वा॥१३॥

verses.sanskrit: त्रीनश्चमेधानत्र त्वं सम्प्राप्य बहुदक्षिणान्। ज्ञातिवध्याकृतं पापं प्रहास्यसि नराधिप॥१५॥
verses.english: Acquiring the merits then of three HorseSacrifices, each with profuse presents, you shall be freed, O king, from the sin of having killed your kinsmen.

verses.sanskrit: पवित्रं परमं चैतत्पावनं चैतदुत्तमम्। यदाश्वमेधावभृथं प्राप्स्यसे कुरुनन्दन॥१६॥
verses.english: The bath which one performs upon completion of the Horse-Sacrifice, O king, is highly powerful and productive of the highest merit. That merit will be yours, O king of Kuru's race. are

verses.sanskrit: इत्युक्तः स तु तेजस्वी व्यासेनामितबुद्धिना। दीक्षां विवेश धर्मात्मा वाजिमेधाप्तये ततः॥१७॥
verses.english: Thus addressed by Vyasa of incomparable intelligence, the righteous-souled Yudhishthria of great energy underwent the initiation for performance of the Horse-Sacrifice.

verses.sanskrit: ततो यज्ञं महाबाहुर्वाजिमेधं महाक्रतुम्। बह्वन्नदक्षिणं राजा सर्वकामगुणान्वितम्॥१८॥
verses.english: The mighty-armed king then performed the great Horse-Sacrifice characterised by gifts of food and presents in profusion and capable of fructifying every desire and producing cvery merit.

verses.sanskrit: तत्र वेदविदो राजंश्चक्रुः कर्माणि याजकाः। परिक्रमन्तः सर्वज्ञा विधिवत्साधुशिक्षितम्॥१९॥
verses.english: The priests, well-conversant with the Vedas, did every rite, duly, moving about in all directions. They were all well-trained, and possessed of omniscience.

verses.sanskrit: न तेषां स्खलितं किञ्चिदासीच्चाप्यकृतं तथा। क्रममुक्तं च युक्तं च चक्रुस्तत्र द्विजर्षभाः॥२०॥
verses.english: In nothing was there any deviation from the ordinances, and nothing was done improperly. Those foremost of twice-born persons followed the procedure as laid down as it should be followed in those points about which no directions are given.

verses.sanskrit: कृत्वा प्रवर्ग्यं धर्माख्यं यथावद्द्विजसत्तमाः। चक्रुस्ते विधिवद्राजंस्तथैवाभिषवं द्विजाः॥२१॥
अभिषूय ततो राजन्सोमं सोमपसत्तमाः। सवनान्यानुपूर्व्येण चक्रुः शास्त्रानुसारिणः॥२२॥
न तत्र कृपणः कश्चिन्न दरिद्रो बभूव ह। क्षुधितो दुःखितो वापि प्राकृतो वापि मानवः॥२३॥
verses.english: Among those who came to that sacrifice none could be seen who was cheerless, none who was poor, none who was hungry, none who was plunged into grief, and none that seemed to be vulgar.

verses.sanskrit: भोजनं भोजनार्थिभ्यो दापयामास शत्रुहा। भीमसनो महातेजाः सततं राजशासनात्॥२४॥
verses.english: Bhimasena of great energy, at the command of the king, caused food to be ceaselessly distributed among those who desired to eat.

verses.sanskrit: संस्तरे कुशलाश्चापि सर्वकार्याणि याजकाः। दिवसे दिवसे चक्रुर्यथाशास्त्रानुदर्शनात्॥२५॥
verses.english: Following the injunctions of the scriptures, priests, well-versed in sacrificial rites of every kind, performed every day all the acts necessary to complete the great sacrifice.

verses.sanskrit: नाषडङ्गविदत्रासीत्सदस्यस्तस्य धीमतः। नाव्रतो नानुपाध्यायो न च वादाविचक्षणः॥२६॥
verses.english: Amongst the Sadasyas of king Yudhishthira of great intelligence there was none who was not a master of the six branches of (Vedic) learning. There was none among them who was not an otserver of vows, none who was not an Upadhaya; none, who was not wellversed in dialectical disputations.

verses.sanskrit: ततो यूपोछ्रये प्राप्ते षड्बैल्वान्भरतर्षभ। खादिरान् बिल्वसमितांस्तावतः सर्ववर्णिनः॥२७॥
verses.english: When the time came for erccting the sacrificial stake, O chief of Bharata's race, six stakes were set up which were made of Bilva, six which were made of Khadira, and six which were made of Sarvavarnin.

verses.sanskrit: देवदारुमयौ द्वौ तु यूपौ कुरुपतेर्मखे। श्लेष्मातकमयं चैकं याजका: समकल्पयन्॥२८॥
verses.english: Two stakes were set up by the priest which were made of Devadaru in that sacrifice of the Kuru king, and one which was made of Shleshmataka.

verses.sanskrit: शोभार्थं चापरान्यूपान्काञ्चनान्भरतर्षभ। स भीमः कारयामास धर्मराजस्य शासनात्॥२९॥
verses.english: At the bchest of the king, Bhima caused some other stakes to be set up, for the sake of beauty only which were made of goid.

verses.sanskrit: ते व्यराजन्त राजर्षेर्वासोभिरुपशोभिताः। महेन्द्रानुगता देवा यथा सप्तर्षिभिर्दिवि॥३०॥
verses.english: Adorned with fine cloths supplied by the royal sage, those stakes shone there like Indra and the deities with the seven celestial Rishis standing around them in Heaven.

verses.sanskrit: इष्टकाः काञ्चनीश्चात्र चयनार्थं कृताऽभवन्। शुशुभे चयनं तच्च दक्षस्येव प्रजापतेः॥३१॥
verses.english: A number of golden bricks were made for making therewith a Chayana. The Chayana made resembled in beauty that which had been made for Daksha, the lord of creatures.

verses.sanskrit: चतुश्चित्यश्च तस्यासीदष्टादशकरात्मकः। स रुक्मपक्षो निचितस्त्रिकोणो गरुडाकृतिः॥३२॥
verses.english: The Chayana measured eight and ten cubits and had four stories or lairs. A golden bird, of the shape of Garuda, was then made, having three angles.

verses.sanskrit: ततो नियुक्ताः पशवो यथाशास्त्रं मनीषिभिः। तं तं देवं समुद्दिश्य पक्षिणः पशवश्च ये॥३३॥
verses.english: Following the injunctions of the scriptures, the priests endued with great learning then duly tied to the stakes both animals and birds, assigning each to its particular deity.

verses.sanskrit: ऋषभाः शास्त्रपठितास्तथा जलचराश्च ये। सर्वांस्तानभ्ययुञ्जस्ते तत्राग्निचयकर्मणि॥३४॥
verses.english: Bulls, possessed of such marks as are mentioned in the scriptures, and aquatic animals were properly tied to the stakes after the rites of the sacrificial fire had been performed.

verses.sanskrit: यूपेषु नियता चासीत्पशूनां त्रिशती तथा। अश्वरत्नोत्तरा यज्ञे कौन्तेयस्य महात्मनः॥३५॥
verses.english: In that sacrifice of the great son of Kunti, three hundred animals were tied to the stakes set up, including that foremost of horses.

verses.sanskrit: स यज्ञः शुशुभे तस्य साक्षाद्देवर्षिसङ्कुलः। गन्धर्वगणसङ्गीतः प्रवृत्तोप्सरसां गणैः॥३६॥
verses.english: That sacrifice looked greatly beautiful as if adorned with the celestial Rishis, with the Gandharvas singing in chorus and the various tribes of Apsaras dancing in merriment.

verses.sanskrit: स किम्पुरुषसङ्कीर्णः किन्नरैश्चोपशोभितः। सिद्धविप्रनिवासैश्च समन्तादभिसंवृतः॥३७॥
verses.english: It teemed, besides, with Kimpurushas and was adorned with Kinnaras. All around it were houses of Brahinanas crowned with ascetic success.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मिन्सदसि नित्यास्तु व्यासशिष्या द्विजर्षभाः। सर्वशास्त्रप्रणेतारः कुशला यज्ञसंस्तरे॥३८॥
verses.english: There were daily seen the disciples of Vyasa, those foremost of twice-born ones, who are compilers of all branches of learning, and well conversant with sacrificial rites.

verses.sanskrit: नारदश्च बभूवात्र तुम्बुरश्च महाद्युतिः। विश्वावसुश्चित्रसेनस्तथान्ये गीतकोविदाः॥३९॥
verses.english: There was Narada, and there was Tunburu of great splendour. There were Vishvavasu and Chitrasena and others, all of whom were proficient in music.

verses.sanskrit: गन्धर्वा गीतकुशला नृत्येषु च विशारदाः। रमयन्ति स्म तान्विप्रान् यज्ञकर्मान्तरेषु वै॥४०॥
verses.english: At intervals of the sacrificial rites, those Gandharvas skilled in music and well-versed in dancing, used to please the Brahmanas who were engaged in the sacrifice.
